title: Motor-role phase tests gave no clear separation after correction in ten inputs to one leech motor neuron
abstract: We tested whether five excitatory motor-role inputs and five inhibitory motor-role inputs to leech motor neuron DE-3R had different activity phases. Anatomy and voltage imaging came from the same ganglion. We compared mean unit phasors and used all 252 balanced input-label assignments as an exact reference. Mean squared separation was 0.3467 in two swim trials and 1.1971 in three left-bend trials. Exact p values were 0.3571 and 0.03175. After Holm correction across both scores and their contrast, p values were 0.3571, 0.09524, and 0.2222. No planned test passed 0.05. Contact weighting increased the descriptive scores to 0.7991 and 2.1164. One input supplied 52 of 66 inhibitory-role contacts. Its group had only 1.576 effective equal-weight inputs under an independent equal-variance noise model. These results show how contact weights can change an activity summary. They do not establish a general motor-role phase rule. One animal, ten selected inputs, a cell-name conflict, dependent signals, and absent raw trace errors limit inference. Motor role does not establish the sign of each central synapse. We provide source hashes, code, derived data, exact label scores, figures, and independent checks.
